column1: # THE BRIDGE. A SEMANTIC token this engine's stylesheets already read, and the
# canonical PRIMITIVE that should supply it.
# Emitted by docrender/theme.py into :root, AFTER the local base rows and AFTER
# the canonical vectors, as `--dr-<consumer>: var(--dr-<canonical>)`.
# WHY THIS EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS NOT A SECOND VOCABULARY
# The stylesheets were never full of raw numbers everywhere -- they already read
# tokens for the things that matter most. Those tokens are SEMANTIC: `lede-size`
# means "the opening paragraph", `spec-label` means "a field name in a generated
# spec table". The canonical vectors are PRIMITIVES: `fs-lead`, `fs-xs`.
# A semantic name is the right thing for a stylesheet to read -- it says WHY,
# and it survives the primitive behind it changing. So the join between the two
# layers is a rename, and this is the rename table.
# STAR THIS IS THE THIRD USE OF THE SAME PATTERN. Colour aliases (`--dr-ink:
# var(--dr-text)`) did it per-scheme; the local-underneath layering does it for
# tokens canonical does not model; this does it for the scheme-independent
# vectors. Same argument every time: keep the consumer's vocabulary, point it at
# the canonical value, never find-and-replace across the asset layer.
# WARNING: A ROW HERE CHANGES WHAT A PAGE LOOKS LIKE. It is not plumbing.
# WARNING: ONLY MAP A GENUINE EQUIVALENT. A near-miss forced into a row is worse
# than an honest gap: it looks wired, it renders wrong, and nothing reports it.
# `measure` has no canonical primitive and is therefore NOT here.
# TWO ROWS WERE CUT ON 2026-08-05, AND THE TEST THEY FAILED IS THE ONE DIRECTLY
# ABOVE THIS BLOCK. Michael, on the published desktop table: "the font in the
# TABLE is massive and the table columns don't fit right." Both halves were
# these two rows.
#   data-pad -> pad-cell     A DIMENSION MISMATCH, not a near miss. The local
#     value is `0.34rem 0.6rem`: TWO axes, 5.4px vertical and 9.6px horizontal,
#     and the asymmetry is the entire point -- a data row wants to be SHORT so
#     more rows fit and WIDE so columns separate. `pad-cell` is ONE number, so
#     `tight` (8px) made every row 48% taller and every column 17% narrower at
#     the same time. A one-axis primitive cannot express a two-axis value, and
#     no amount of choosing a better spacing entity fixes that.
#     ⚠️ Its own note called it "the single highest-leverage row here" and that
#     was the argument FOR it. Leverage is the reason a mismatch here is the
#     most expensive kind, not the reason to take it.
#   data-size -> fs-sm       The note read "Local 0.80rem -> sharp-racing 0.8rem.
#     Byte-different, visually identical." True of sharp-racing. This site does
#     not render sharp-racing. ⚠️ A BRIDGE ROW DOES NOT HAVE ONE VALUE -- it has
#     one per theme, and only one of them was ever measured. A row is safe when
#     it is safe under EVERY entity a join can name, and nothing here checks
#     that.
# ⭐ WHAT GENERALISES, FOR THE NEXT ROW SOMEBODY WANTS TO ADD: a token that a
# DENSE surface reads is not the same question as the primitive a page reads,
# even when both are "padding" or both are "a small font size". Table density is
# a property of the table. It belongs to theme/typography.tsv, where it can be
# stated per theme and per axis, and where `database` and `eos` already state it.
# consumer    the semantic token the stylesheets already read
# canonical   the primitive that now supplies it
# vector      which canonical vector it comes from
# note        what the value was, what it becomes, and where it shows
consumer
lede-size
column4: The opening paragraph, and the search snippet. Local 1.15rem (18.4px) -> whatever the theme's typography entity sets; sharp-racing is 1rem (16px), so ledes get slightly tighter on this site. Single axis, one question, safe under any entity.
